Experiment claims use cold matched runs, base-commit provenance, namespaced identities, explicit schemas, deterministic gates, price-aware arithmetic, and replay evidence demotion.
The acknowledged doubled work is bounded by utilization thresholds, per-window and weekly caps, kill controls, and skipped execution when quota facts are unavailable.

Checked filesystem writes, persisted fields, telemetry scope, and live content handling; writes use a fail-closed allowlist, raw project content is not persisted, and automatic config writes are excluded.

The ADR labels marker coincidence after surfacing as proof that the recommended snippet was applied, although the matcher establishes only that independently matchable heading and phrase fragments exist.
Transition detection is centralized once in the engine loop, efficacy reuses the existing replay stack and budget, and no per-detector sweep or parallel measurement pipeline is introduced.
Domain-taxonomy decision; it introduces no auth, filesystem, network, client, command, container, or secret boundary.
The detector design rejects bare latency statistics, requires an attributable clock lever, separates latency from retry/queue inflation, and keeps unsupported measurements as raw stats.
It classifies performance recommendations but does not itself add hot-path code or a shipped runtime surface.
Checked filesystem and container boundaries, artifact privacy, dependency placement, and mount exposure; generation stays host-side, the container is read-only, and source bodies are excluded.
The parser contract requires source-free structured artifacts, hashes/mtimes, a git-SHA or root-mtime staleness stamp, visible stale badges, schemas, and test assertions.
Generation is outside request handling, rendered output has a configurable tested token cap, and caching/invalidation is explicitly assigned to the consumer slice.

findings.title: Marker coincidence is overstated as proof that the recommended fix was applied
findings.what: The ADR calls a FIRING→SUPPRESSED marker transition deterministic evidence that the finding caused a change and that the fix snippet was applied, then reports the state as ADOPTED. The marker contract only establishes that a matching heading and case-insensitive phrase fragments exist somewhere in merged CLAUDE.md after the finding was surfaced. Those fragments can be written independently, pre-exist in a different merged scope, or arrive for an unrelated reason; temporal ordering does not prove that the recommendation caused or exactly supplied the change. The lower-bound caveat addresses missed adoptions but not these false-positive attribution paths.
findings.fix: Rename the measured state and aggregate to marker-confirmed suppression or configuration alignment, and state that it is evidence consistent with adoption rather than proof of recommendation-caused application. Reserve ADOPTED/coached attribution for an explicit user action receipt or a verified before/after hunk tied to the surfaced finding.
findings.acceptance: A documentation check confirms that the cited sections no longer say markers prove the snippet was applied or that the finding caused the change; cards and aggregates use non-causal marker-confirmed terminology unless the design adds an explicit action receipt or tied before/after diff as required evidence.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the cited passages and compared them with the baseline matcher. The related implementation merges global and per-project CLAUDE.md text, accepts any matching heading regex, and checks body phrases using case-insensitive substring inclusion; it does not verify an exact pasted snippet, a localized hunk, authorship, or causation. The candidate therefore survives as a reproducible claim-semantics defect rather than a style objection.
